Cc: compliance@medsentry.com

Subject: CAIQ + TTL carveout request for MedSentry (follow-up)

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance and security team dug into the CAIQ and had two related asks we need to close before our procurement committee can sign off:

1) Log retention TTL: Our policy requires audit logs for tenant activity to be retained for 18 months for regulatory reasons in a couple of our EU/US hybrid products. Your public docs reference a 90-day default for ephemeral session and debug logs. Can Redwood provide a customer-specific TTL carveout for a named tenant (MedSentry) — i.e., extend session/audit logs to 18 months for that tenant only? If so, what controls or compensating controls do you require (e.g., VPC private deploy, dedicated capacity, encryption-at-rest KMS, access approvals)?

2) CAIQ evidence: For the CAIQ sections that reference logging and retention (SIG / CAIQ: LOG-xx), could you provide a one-page summary of which artifacts you can produce (SOC 2 attestations, configured TTLs, export playbooks, screenshots of retention settings, and a sample export) and an estimated ETA?

We can accept partial evidence first (e.g., a CSV export of a 30-day sample with redaction) while a longer-term attestation is processed.

Can you confirm feasibility and an initial timeline by EOD Wednesday? We have a procurement review on Thursday.

Thanks,
Danielle Park
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedSentry Health

Subject: Re: CAIQ + TTL carveout request for MedSentry (follow-up)

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can support a tenant-scoped retention extension, but the implementation and evidence path depend on deployment mode. High level: 

- Hosted (multi-tenant): tenant-specific, long-term retention is possible via account-level archival exports (customer export bucket) + configured retention policy, but it requires a signed Data Processing Addendum and a brief ops change window. We typically gate this behind an enterprise contract.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): straightforward — we can set the node-level TTL and preserve audit logs for 18 months. Recommended for your use case.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control, no additional Redwood gating.

Compensating controls we typically require for 18-month retention on hosted: dedicated ingestion namespace, encryption with customer KMS, and restricted access via RBAC + audited service accounts. If you can accept a managed export model (we write nightly exports to your pre-provisioned S3 with customer-managed encryption), time-to-live is enforced by your bucket lifecycle rather than our ephemeral tiers.

For CAIQ evidence: we can produce the following deliverables in stages:
1) Stage 1 (48–72 hrs): CAIQ section-level answers + a one-page artifact list, sample CSV export (30-day redacted), and screenshots of retention configuration.
2) Stage 2 (7–10 days): SOC 2-related attestation extract and a formal log-retention attestation letter signed by our security lead.
3) Stage 3 (3–4 weeks): Ops playbook for exports, signed contract addendum (if applicable), and an implementation walkthrough.

I’ll coordinate with Ops to confirm the exact export shape and get you a sample by Tuesday EOD. Sean, can you weigh in on the hosted export cadence and whether we need to route this to Dedicated sales to expedite the TTL change?

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Irene / Marissa — quick ops note: for hosted customers we can deliver the nightly export to a customer bucket (encrypted with their KMS) within 2 business days after the DPA/carveout is signed. The export contains: tenant_id, event_ts, actor_id (hashed), event_type, event_payload (redacted). It is append-only and we keep an internal index for 90 days by default.

If MedSentry needs 18 months of searchable logs served from Redwood, that triggers a Dedicated capacity recommendation — we can preserve KV cache artefacts for a longer window but searching back >90 days on hosted is export-based (i.e., you query your S3 exports).

Action items:
- Irene: provide CAIQ summary + sample export by Tue 10/27 (stage 1)
- Marissa: draft the DPA addendum and pricing delta for nightly export + storage (estimate)
- Sean: create an ops runbook stub and confirm sample columns (will attach to JIRA SEC-4592)

I'll also add a short note on compensating controls we want enforced for hosted: dedicated namespace, KMS, and service-account approval flow.

Sean Gallagher
